guards.name: dashboard-wire-boundary
guards.invariant: Ref frontend-backend-integration §8.2/§8.3/§8.13 and ref operator-trust §7: src/dashboard declares no handwritten structural mirror of a *Wire contract (schema-inferred types only), no dashboard file carries a registered workflow-id string literal — workflow identity reaches surfaces only as SERVED data, never as a branchable literal — and the bundled-import closure of EVERY *.html entry under src/dashboard reaches no Node built-in, so a shared domain contract can never drag node:path/node:fs/node:crypto into a browser bundle. 2i-F/D175 generalised that arm from the single hardcoded index.html to every entry, and added the phone-scope arm: the capture.html entry's closure may not reach src/dashboard/surfaces/**, src/dashboard/client/** or src/dashboard/app/**, because the capture ingress is ref operator-trust §7's ONE exception to loopback-only and serves that page's own asset closure — a single transitive import would ship the run detail, the command envelope and the SSE transport to a public origin without touching a route. Both arms carry negative controls: the config resolver's real node:crypto/node:path reach, and the operator entry's legitimate reach into all three forbidden roots. D264/D11 added the registry-reach arm: no *.html entry's closure may reach src/workflows/** or src/control/**. D251 had let the Run Modal read summary/enqueue/surfaces.inputRun off the bundle-safe WORKFLOW_DESCRIPTORS tuple because those three are plain data, and the price was never measured — the tuple pulls every registered workflow's whole graph, node specs, task contracts and src/base/** builders, so the browser downloaded the composition root to render three fields (1,114,214 bytes; 753,197 after). The three are now served as WorkflowStartWireSchema and this arm holds the tuple out; it too carries a negative control — the walker's real resolution into src/workflows/** from the registry itself. D274 item 3 added the specimen-bundle arm (ledger 3 UK146-UK157): the kit.html entry's TS/TSX import closure may not reach src/dashboard/surfaces/**, client/**, state/**, app/** or phone/**, because the design-system specimen page's whole claim is that what it renders is the SYSTEM drawn against synthetic literals - a reach into a surface would present one surface's composition of a primitive as the primitive's own behaviour, and a reach into the client would put a served fact on a page whose premise is that it serves none. src/domain/** stays reachable on purpose (ds/primitives-status.tsx reads the shared status vocabulary). CARVE-OUT: kit/main.tsx deliberately imports app/index.css so the --ds-* layer resolves against the real app theme; the walker resolves only .ts/.tsx specifiers (a .css specifier never matches a resolvable candidate), so this import is invisible to the closure walk and does not trip the app/** arm — a fact about the walker's reach, not an exemption from it, and worth stating because the arm's own text would otherwise read as contradicted by that import. Its negative control is the operator entry's legitimate reach into four of the five roots, proven for app/** via a non-entry file (dashboard-app.tsx) rather than the entry file itself, which already sits under app/** and would pass the check vacuously. The same commit added the build-input arm: every *.html entry the walker guards must also appear as a rollup input in vite.dashboard.config.ts, because a page that only renders on the dev server is a page ref frontend-backend-integration §7's parity lane - which serves dist/dashboard statically - can never photograph.

guards.name: legacy-capability-disposition

guards.name: legacy-change-accounting

guards.name: migration-history-immutability

guards.name: config-snapshot-generations
guards.invariant: The durable config leaf set is SHA-256 pinned per generation: adding or tightening a required config leaf without registering it in CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATIONS and bumping CURRENT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATION fails here. guards.name: settings-catalog
guards.invariant: D331 P1/P2/P5/P8/P33: the closed 88-row settings registry covers every ordinary config leaf, protected entry, provider-key family, host-derived publication and runtime-isolation channel in both directions; each row has one legal sensitivity/source-class pairing, only existing named consumers, and one contract-owned restart scope. guards.name: no-secret-values-in-logs

guards.name: operational-isolation
guards.invariant: Both runtimes on this machine bind distinct commands, state/artifact roots, ports, process locks, and browser profiles/sessions; exact legacy launch scripts are frozen with commit/blob provenance rather than read from an external checkout, and the rebuild's isolation values come from one exported direct-const defineRuntimeIsolation call that a composition root invokes at top level through unshadowed named imports.

guards.name: operator-mutation-admission
guards.invariant: Ref frontend-backend-integration §3.4 (D75, 2026-09-02): every browser-reachable mutating route the BFF registers in src/server/dashboard/routes/api.ts is admitted by a loopback Host/Origin door BEFORE its handler runs, per a closed admission table — JSON-envelope doors (commands, bulk, XLSX export, start plans, Explorer validation) also require application/json; opaque doors (intake bytes, the body-less advisory) own their media contract; the one inline door (preflight rerun) is named as such. guards.name: parity-reference-authority
guards.invariant: D132: the ref frontend-backend-integration §7 parity lane can fail. Stored .a11y.yml/.meta.json references are compared, never rewritten, on a normal run — an accessibility-only change fails with a diff naming the reference and leaves the file untouched; refreshing requires PARITY_UPDATE=1 (npm run test:parity:update), the same single switch that drives Playwright's updateSnapshots so the pixel and semantic halves of a pair can never be refreshed independently. The served dist/dashboard must carry a build stamp binding both the working-tree source digest and the emitted output digest; a stale, unstamped, or post-build-edited bundle is refused before a port is bound. D145: the pixel half allows ZERO moved pixels (maxDiffPixels: 0) and pins its per-pixel colour tolerance explicitly — the old maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.001 was uncalibrated, hid a 112-px visible content change, and because updateSnapshots: "changed" reuses the same comparison it also stopped test:parity:update from repairing eight pairs whose .a11y.yml had refreshed while their .png stayed stale. No parity spec or helper may set its own screenshot allowance. All arms are executed against violating fixtures and through the lane's own captureA11yReference/startFixtureServer entry points.

guards.name: runtime-dependency-coverage
guards.invariant: The closed browser-system and vision-provider sets, their capabilities, endpoint preflight checks, secret families, and provider-model environment keys agree with the exact frozen legacy inventory and with each other in both directions; the registry self-audit runs in the architecture lane and finished gates never require an external checkout.

guards.name: runtime-environment-coverage
guards.invariant: Every direct, computed, test-only, and documented environment read is explicitly classified; config and secret ownership remain bidirectionally complete.

guards.name: secrets-single-source

guards.name: strict-boundary-schemas
guards.invariant: Every cataloged external or durable boundary is schema-derived, recursively strict across object/union/lazy members, and rejects nested unknown keys and unsafe type/parser escape hatches.

guards.name: test-runtime-root-isolation
guards.invariant: No test may create, mutate, or delete a path rooted at a real runtime-isolation root (the isolation binding's state/artifact/lock/browser-profile properties, or a .auth*/.tracker* literal), directly or through a local binding; a test that constructs the real worker session factory must bind its own non-real paths.browserProfileRoot.

guards.name: test-target-registry
guards.invariant: Ref guards-and-tests §10.5/§10.9: the guard WALKS every tests/scenario/workflows/*/dry-run.scenario.ts, evaluates each declaration without importing it, and requires it to parse, to name only node ids its own descriptor declares, and to be registered in src/cli.ts at its own path in both directions; every T1b manifest case's (label, workflow, kind) matches an ARM of a strict registry entry, and every registry arm has a case in that workflow's own manifest (both directions, D284); the committed registry holds exactly one separations subject, `finalization-canary`, with a `separations` full-chain-dry-run arm and a `separations-kuali-finalization` ordinary arm, pins its dated availability and exactly the three declared-pending finalization leaves (transactionNumber, timekeeperComments, terminationEffectiveDate) that make the standalone resolver answer blocked BY NAME, and commits no observations from a retired document; D300 — the chain arm commits the CLOSED document-number reference (name + literal env key) and never a number, neither arm commits a Kuali document number, the test-target secret registry carries only the closed separations document-number and Person Lookup EID references, the retired secretInput block is gone from the finalization arm, and the finalization resolver has no ready path and no env parameter at all, so it cannot spend a credential; the checked-in export is recursively frozen (references included) and real EIDs cannot enter publicInput. Every entry names a workflow the generated build manifest actually built and records a purpose, and both resolvers answer from the one subject's own arm without cross-workflow guessing.

guards.name: ai-advisory-no-authority
guards.invariant: D178 (ref operator-trust §4.4): optional AI assistance reads the evidence and never becomes it. ZERO AUTHORITY EDGE — the advisory closure's VALUE-import graph (domain/trust/advisory, domain/dashboard/advisory, services/trust/advisory, infra/providers/gemini-advisory, server/dashboard/queries/advisory) may not reach any authority writer (the sqlite repositories, the command kernel, terminal authorization, the write sequencer/recovery, the receipt writer, run-failure, the diagnostic/knowledge/notification services, the ledger, the command services, either composition root, or control), and no command-family module (domain/commands, core/command-kernel, server/dashboard/commands/**) may import an advisory module — so an advisory value cannot cross into a command payload from either direction. A type-only import of a record SHAPE is deliberately not a path to that record's writer. The ONE permitted durable neighbour is D112 provider admission, at the composition root only. DECLARED REDACTION — every leaf a maximal FailureRecord presents carries a declaration and every declaration is exercised by it (both directions), no declaration pairs a classification with a transform redaction.ts forbids, only `safe-diagnostic` may leave as a VALUE, and an undeclared leaf refuses BY NAME rather than being dropped. ADVICE SHAPE — the closed advice schema exposes exactly headline/explanation/checks/confidence and strictly refuses retryability, a remediation kind, a run reference or a command. ROUTE — the advisory is its own POST /api/v1/runs/:runId/advisory, is never a run-detail section (a section would spend a provider budget on panel open), and no command-service module reaches the advisory query. Every arm runs against a violating fixture as well as the real subject.

guards.name: archive-invariants
guards.invariant: D179 (charter §25 / ref dashboard-surfaces §10.2): the D80 archive is a durable, self-contained, insert-only record. The archived-run READ path may not value-reach the workflow registry anywhere in its import closure — checked over the closure rather than one file, and executed against a checked-in violating fixture that reaches `src/base/workflow.ts` two hops away through a re-export, so a walker that resolved nothing could not pass. `version_bump_applications`, `archived_runs` and `archive_relaunches` abort every UPDATE and DELETE in SQL, proved by raw statements against a real migrated database with the rows present (an empty table would pass by doing nothing). No archive module names a `ledger/` PATH, and the only ledger IMPORT any of them may carry is the read-only read-through the archived-detail query calls — a `ledgerPartitions` POINTER field is the opposite of a violation, and resolving one back to the line it names is what keeps the pointer honest. The read-through itself is checked to name no write primitive, because a “repair” there would rewrite the record of what was really filed. The archived record's `contentDigest` is a fixed point over its own content, a tampered record digests differently, and a canonical round trip reproduces it — without which the `archiveFingerprint` a relaunch cites would be decoration. The five behavioural clauses of the exit criterion are pinned in tests/unit/archive-model.test.ts. D223's frozen section payloads are bound to the record's own `archiveSchemaGeneration` in BOTH directions: a reader admits a generation-1 record (those bytes are on disk and nothing may back-fill them) and a WRITER may not produce one, so a build that could not freeze the sections cannot record its own failure as "this record predates them"; a generation-1 record's canonical bytes are proved to gain no `sections` key and to hash to the digest it was written with, which is why the generation bump needed no migration.

guards.name: artifact-effect-boundary
guards.invariant: Artifact references expose stable UUID identity plus immutable digest/size/media type and no root or path; the real writer accepts only a non-symlinked rebuild-isolated artifact root, writes one metadata+payload object via temp→file-fsync→atomic-rename→directory-fsync, recovers cleanly across injected boundaries, returns the same ref for byte-identical content, and keeps task/workflow implementations away from direct mutable filesystem primitives.

guards.name: atomic-write-outbox
guards.invariant: Phase 1c atomic authority commit updates the fenced intent and attempt and inserts one schema-valid ledger outbox plus one terminal-span/generic-outcome outbox in one outer authority transaction; injected failure after every storage step rolls back every change and leaves authority generation unchanged. Browser sequencing and projection remain deferred to Phase 1f.

guards.name: authority-target-no-fallback
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): the invariant is held, and held harder, by `storage-recovery`. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: `AuthorityDatabase.open` refuses an existing-but-empty file by name rather than replacing it, `inspectExistingReadOnly` refuses a schema that is not exactly the supported version, and `storage-recovery` executes the whole family — corrupt, truncated, newer-schema, foreign-key-invalid, invariant-invalid and record-invalid files all open DEGRADED READ-ONLY with a named cause and zero bytes written. D181 added the restore half over a real-shaped copied database. A separate guard could only re-assert what those arms already execute against real SQLite files.

guards.name: bounded-task-deadline
guards.invariant: Every task invocation in the Phase-1 interpreter runs under a mandatory, immutable, scheduler-armed abortable deadline (ref execution-and-sessions §5 item 5): taskDeadlineMs is a required dependency with no default, both invocation arms race the deadline controller, and a task that ignores its signal still lands terminal failed with the wedged session poison-closed.

guards.name: canonical-input-snapshot
guards.invariant: Every registered canonical-input schema is transform-free anywhere in its graph and round-trips its ingress samples; a corrupted snapshot fails loud instead of being re-derived from ingress; and a snapshot only crosses schema hashes through a checked-in, factory-sealed, acyclic migration chain.

guards.name: capture-durability-and-scope
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D294 (2026-08-31): the mobile document-capture product, including its page, ingress routes, command family, session authority and configuration, was removed. Its retirement boundary is now held by `phone-capture-retired`; diagnostic bundle screenshots, run-detail captures and Archive resources remain separately supported evidence surfaces.

guards.name: phone-capture-retired
guards.invariant: D294: no retired mobile document-capture page, phone module, /api/v1/capture route, capture command/wire, session repository, or capture configuration may return. The real tree and a violating fixture are checked; diagnostic bundle screenshots, run-detail captures and Archive resource verification remain required evidence surfaces.

guards.name: commit-routes-through-mutation
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): held by `task-driver-boundary`, which refuses a `commit` implementation outside a store driver owner that validates its capability AND refuses premature capability forgery, both against a checked-in violating fixture. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: the capability itself became runtime-unforgeable at D127 — a module-private WeakSet in `src/core/write-sequencer.ts` is the sole mint and drivers verify with `assertSequencerMintedMutationCapability` — so routing is enforced by construction and the guard only has to keep the allowlist honest.

guards.name: control-command-single-path
guards.invariant: D113/D283/D331: exactly one command kernel executes ref dashboard-surfaces's command protocol — journal and audit writes are statically confined to it. The two settings authority verifiers may perform only their exact read-only commandAudits.findByCommand calls: two runtime document authentications and three copied-backup/manifest authentications; neither can insert, mutate or infer an outcome. Every family/action dispatches to a typed result with active arms executing and deferred arms rejected capability-unavailable with zero authority-generation advance. Command ids replay byte-exactly. Explorer durable apply is one typed active arm carrying descriptor version/fingerprint plus override revision; it retains actor/source audit and invokes its external file executor once across a journaled replay. Every run verb CASes the CALLER's expected version with no exceptions — presentation (D233 — a stale rename may not overwrite a current name) and bump included; typed gate results parse the descriptor result schema before storage; notification stays read/unread/snooze; capture targets cannot spell a run id; and an injected active-run lookup failure enqueues zero runs.

guards.name: delegation-manifest
guards.invariant: Delegation edge ids are unique per workflow; one D102 policy vocabulary spans builder, manifest, dependency row, and UI; the plan fingerprint covers edge, cardinality, join, policy, and every child id and input; a drifted replay fails loud; a join runs only over the complete outcome set; and a zero-child fan-out stays an explicit satisfied join with a writable durable manifest.

guards.name: descriptor-coverage
guards.invariant: Ref workflow-model §1.4: one table-driven sweep over DESCRIPTORS — unique ids/codes/icons, the module tuple agreeing with every derived registry in both directions, contract placement and examples, the derived browser-system union, concretely typed child-run targets, the bundle-safe value-import closure of every descriptor module, a current build manifest, and descriptor-to-impl pairing tracked explicitly rather than implicitly. The manifest is current in BOTH senses: the parsed manifest equals a fresh recomputation, and the checked-in module text equals the generator's exact bytes — formatting/ordering drift that deepEqual is structurally blind to fails the gate, proven by a negative control that reformats the module and shows the parsed arm stays green. The byte arm is one shared function used by the guard and by `npm run build:manifest:check`, whose presence in package.json is pinned so the `--check` CLI can never again ship wired to nothing. D107's pending-impl bindings are audited in both directions with a live fixture per staleness arm: an entry no descriptor uses, and (D184) an entry a store now implements.

guards.name: driver-lease-boundary
guards.invariant: Drivers exist only inside WorkerSessionManager.withDriver's callback lease: withDriver is consumed only by the graph interpreter, the browser-session factory's open() is invoked only inside worker-sessions, and only the worker loop constructs a WorkerSessionManager ownership scope.

guards.name: dry-run-composition-submit-free
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): held by `write-safety-contract` plus the executable scenario `separations-kuali-finalization/dry-run-preview`, which runs the REAL write sequencer over a REAL authority database and asserts zero write-authority/output deltas — zero `write_intents`, zero `write_attempts`, and zero `durable_outbox` rows — rather than inspecting a composition for the absence of a call. Ordinary upstream task `run_checkpoints` still exist in a dry run and are required to reach the preview boundary; they are not write evidence. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: `executeDryRun` is a separate arm and `executeTransaction` with `dryRun` refuses loudly, so a submit-free dry run is a property of the kernel's shape, and the scenario is what proves it on rows.

guards.name: edit-data-field-policy
guards.invariant: Edit Data's default is read-only: a descriptor must declare every correctable node+field path, a declared path must resolve through the producing READ task node's own output schema (a transaction node's output is a write proof and never correctable), the negative controls run through the real descriptor factory, every registered descriptor's policy parses the closed schema, and the edit-checkpoint save command stays in the ACTIVE partition so a declared policy can never outrun the kernel arm whose CAS-against-resume-fence honours it (D166).

guards.name: evidence-receipt
guards.invariant: A terminal run's receipt is strict at every level and carries the graph/config/input fingerprints, a source and observation instant for every fact, a filed binding proof for every verified write, and one explicit confidence; `verified-done` is refused for non-verified confidence, an unresolved mandatory fact or obligation, any warning, or a failure id, each proven by a violating fixture. Redaction is DECLARED: every leaf of every registered canonical-input sample and every used contract's sealed example carries a classification whose transform its classification permits, an undeclared leaf fails loud rather than dropping, a declaration that disagrees with domain/secrets.ts fails, and no env key, cookie, storage-state, or raw-SSN canary reaches a built receipt. The diagnostic-bundle half of ref guards-and-tests §3.10 activates with the bundle capture slice. D199 — a receipt is bound to the surfaces its derivation CONSUMES, never to the descriptor's source closure: `descriptorFingerprint` is the closure the RUN executed under, read from its own envelope, so a settled receipt re-derives byte-identically after any edit that leaves every consumed surface intact, and a receipt that took the current build's `contractFingerprint` stranded every already-settled run on the next unrelated edit. Resolvability is a named check table — `workflow-identity`, `descriptor-version`, `canonical-input`, `evidence-graph`, `terminal-dependency-set`, `declared-evidence` — printed in full with both fingerprints, `[held]`/`[MOVED]`/`[skip]` distinct and no waiver arm. `declared-evidence` is the one check whose baseline is the stored receipt row, because the declared redaction and obligation tables live OUTSIDE every descriptor closure and can move with `contractFingerprint` byte-identical; the immutable insert stays underneath as the backstop. D204 — a GATE's durable evidence is a `gate_results` row and never a checkpoint, so a resolved gate node emits its payload's leaves as facts sourced `gate-result` (carrying authority's own `resolvedBy`/`resolvedAt`, never a payload claim), ONE `kind: "gate"` decision naming the approver, the instant, the resolving command and the bound evidence digest, and a `verified` obligation in place of the `unknown` a checkpoint-only derivation reported. The outcome is DECLARED per `(workflow, gate)` in `src/domain/trust/gate-decisions.ts` and never sniffed from a field name: every gate node of every registered descriptor has a declaration whose decision and bound-evidence leaves classify under a `gate-result` redaction scope, an undeclared gate and an unlisted arm value both fail loud, an orphan declaration or gate-scoped classification fails, and a foreign run's gate row, a gate that left the graph and an undeclared arm are executed as negative controls against the REAL gated descriptor, and the UNDECLARED `(workflow, gate)` pair — unreachable through the builder precisely because every registered gate node is declared — is pinned directly on `gateDecisionFor`, which is the only route from a stored row to a `DecisionEvidence.outcome`. D270 — an orphan task-output classification is judged against the BUILD MANIFEST task set rather than only the descriptor-reachable one, because observed-log emission redacts by declaration for every task the executor runs and a composed fixture descriptor must borrow a manifest-known id.

guards.name: fresh-session-boundary
guards.invariant: A browser-session boundary is authored or identity-forced, never inferred: the `fresh-boundary` close reason exists only inside the session-ownership modules, every task/workflow `session:` need is a string literal rather than a computed value, repeated reuse-worker needs mint no boundary, and both an authored session:"fresh" need and a D116 (worker,system,resolvedInstance,configFingerprint) reuse-identity mismatch close the old resource with an accepted page/context proof BEFORE the replacement opens and authenticates. The descriptor-level node-execution ordering arm lands with the first workflow that authors a fresh-boundary node.

guards.name: identity-gate-before-commit
guards.invariant: Ref write-safety §14.6 #2: in a separation-class descriptor BOTH sinks — every transaction node and the terminal result — are graph-reachable only through an operator gate. Every dependsOn ancestry path from a sink must reach the gate's own ancestry (the gate plus its transitive dependsOn closure) before a graph root; a node OUTSIDE that ancestry is data the operator never saw at the gate, and a side read feeding the sink is the violation. The terminal arm landed with separations chunk 3 because a read-only chunk produces an APPROVED SUBJECT a later composition binds a write's expected side to, so a terminal result reachable without the gate hands that composition an unconfirmed identity. The registered gate is additionally pinned to ref write-safety §14.4's IdentityApprovalResult schema hash — the exact value executeResolveGate compares an incoming payload against — so §14.6 risk 5 (a gate result becoming free-form control state) is structurally closed. Executed both ways against gated and ungated fixtures, including a synthesized side read.

guards.name: knowledge-fix-integrity
guards.invariant: D139 (ref operator-trust §4, §9): knowledge records carry status/scope/evidence/validity and forward supersession refs, and admission is audited INSIDE the insert transaction because an insert-only table cannot retract a duplicate. Two active records may not claim the same scoped rule — same scope plus same normalized title or a shared regression scenario — without the successor explicitly superseding the predecessor; a supersedes ref that names nothing recorded, a self-reference, and a duplicate id are each refused with the conflict named. The generated per-system KNOWLEDGE.md is the active view alone: superseded, retired, and unverified records never reach it. A verified FixRecord requires a commit plus non-empty verification evidence and a regression scenario, a draft may claim neither, and a verified fix may not link knowledge that is missing or itself unverified. A raw chronological lesson append is not authority: triageLesson has exactly one arm and it returns the obligations still owed, never a record.

guards.name: ledger-projector
guards.invariant: D134 (ref write-safety §6): the ledger is projected by ONE serialized, actor-attributed writer and is never pruned. No module outside src/infra/ledger/ may append the ledger, and no module that can name ledger/ may call a deletion primitive — both arms run against violating fixtures, and pruneEventStreams stays structurally blind to the ledger (EVENT_STREAMS is exactly spans+notes). A line's bytes and digest are a pure function of (outbox payload, seq) with a versioned domain separator, and its partition comes from the entry's own confirmedAt in UTC, never from wall-clock now. Sequence assignment is idempotent by outboxId, burns no sequence on repeat, refuses a conflicting line digest, and refuses any projector that does not hold the exact (system,date) lease generation. A non-dense partition sequence degrades the store read-only at boot, and the projection report's degraded arm is a closed reason set that no projected arm can smuggle.

guards.name: legacy-preservation
guards.invariant: D93: the path->whole-file-SHA preservation manifest existed to decide which legacy files the same-tree scan treated strictly. guards.name: multi-worker-overlap
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED BY D182 (ref execution-and-sessions §7.1 rows C1-C4). More than one REAL `runWorkerLoop` instance, with distinct worker ids, races ONE workflow queue over ONE shared authority database, and the durable claim set is sampled at every span event and every driver call rather than read once at the end. Two facts hold at once and pull in opposite directions: no worker EVER owns two rows in `claimed|validating|running` (ref execution-and-sessions §0.3, sampled live so a double claim released before the end could not hide), and the fleet genuinely overlaps -- the observed maximum of workers holding work simultaneously equals the worker count, which is ref execution-and-sessions §7's 'parallelism silently serializes' risk stated as a measurement. Every enqueued run is executed exactly once, claimed by exactly one worker, and ends terminal `done` at claim generation 1 and attempt 1, so a second claim or a requeue is visible in authority rather than only in a report. A row held by a live loop is never served to a sibling `claimNext` and the holder's own second `claimNext` throws by name. A sweep interleaved with a live heartbeat requeues only the genuinely stale row -- the freshly renewed claim keeps its owner, generation and attempt -- and the requeued row is proved re-claimable by the same live loop. A zombie heartbeat whose row was swept and re-owned reports `lost` and abandons instead of stamping a heartbeat over the new owner.

guards.name: no-lifecycle-sql-outside-the-adapter
guards.invariant: PLANNED for 1.6 Task 4 (D330.10/D332.9): lifecycle mutation and lifecycle-authoritative reads route only through the run-record service adapter; no dashboard, worker, command, executor, or projection seam writes tasks/leases directly or treats evidence and runs_view as lifecycle authority. The guard and its violating fixture activate together only after Task 4 has displaced the existing writers.

guards.name: no-positional-identity
guards.invariant: No durable identity is positional or borrowed: every run, worker, workflow, node, gate, actor, delegation-edge, and extracted-record id rejects an index, an ordinal, and a stringified number, and a UUID cannot be spelled as any slug-shaped id, so a run id can never stand in as a worker id.

guards.name: notification-durability
guards.invariant: D138 (ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6/§10.4 D79b; ref operator-trust §6): a notification is a durable record FIRST and a desktop delivery second. `publish` settles create-or-fold in one authority transaction and only then attempts OS delivery, and the load-bearing arm injects a delivery that throws — the item must still be durably unread with its count and version untouched, because the operator who missed the toast has only the inbox left. No per-attempt delivery state is written. Each of ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6's closed triggers commits an item and routes to its ratified D79b channel (failed/gate-waiting/write-parked/repeating/storage → ping, verified-done → inbox), each carries its own dedupe identity that excludes the occurrence, and a repeat FOLDS into the one (actorId, dedupeFingerprint) row — count up, lastSeenAt advanced, unread again — rather than minting a second. Snooze suppresses delivery only and never flips status; read state and snooze move independently; a stale version is refused. The trigger event union is ids, closed codes, and counts, so notification text has no free-text channel a captured value could enter through.

guards.name: one-projection-counts

guards.name: worker-teardown-soak
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED BY D182 (ref execution-and-sessions §7.1 rows C5-C8). guards.name: explorer-prose-declared

guards.invariant: Ref data-intake-and-edit-data §7 vectors #1/#3/#6/#13. Hooks, pure folds, vocabularies and object/array constants live in a sibling <surface>-model.ts. @vitejs/plugin-react accepts a module as a Fast Refresh boundary only when every export is a component or is reference-equal across re-evaluation, so one exported helper makes every edit to the surface invalidate upward into dashboard-app.tsx and remount the whole app. Both arms run against checked-in fixtures: one violating in every way the rule can break (hook, helper, object constant, array constant, lowercase re-export), one clean (declared, memo'd, forwardRef'd, arrow and re-exported components plus types). src/dashboard/ds/** is out of scope by design — ui.tsx is the one mixed barrel.

guards.name: dashboard-memo-prop-stability
guards.invariant: Track D row D4 (ref frontend-backend-integration §7.4; audit finding P1): QueuePanel, TopBar and LogPanel are memo'd, and no prop slot of those three elements in src/dashboard/app/*.tsx may contain an object literal, an array literal, an arrow function, a function expression or a `new` — the five constructs that are provably a new reference on every evaluation. memo compares by Object.is, so ONE such slot makes the wrapper pure overhead: the panel re-renders exactly as often as before while every gate stays green and no surface looks wrong. Each of the five shipped in dashboard-app.tsx before D4 (an inline nav={{...}}, an inline handlers={{...}} of five closures, dayWire?.queueSurfaces ?? [], an inline onDay closure). A JSX spread is judged THROUGH rather than at, because its object literal is destructured away and never becomes a prop value. The guard deliberately says NOTHING about a call in a prop slot (workflowLabelOf(id)): a call is not provably unstable, and judging one would need either an allowlist that rots or a refusal of honest primitive-returning helpers. A second arm asserts the three components really are memo-wrapped, so the guard cannot end up protecting nothing. Both arms run against checked-in fixtures — one violating in all five ways, one clean — so a walker resolving nothing could not pass.

guards.name: command-result-exhaustive
guards.invariant: D253 (ref frontend-backend-integration §"D253"): every module under src/dashboard/** settles a CommandResult through the ONE exhaustive fold (src/dashboard/app/command-result.ts), never by testing one refusal arm and letting the other fall through. CommandResultSchema has three arms and TWO are refusals — `conflict` (the CAS refusal, carrying the server's currentVersion) and `rejected` (a kernel refusal code). A surface reading `state === "rejected"` alone treats a conflict as success: the Context rail's Data save closed its editor, discarded the operator's drafts and reported a correction SAVED that the kernel had refused on a version check, and the notification bell swallowed a stale-revision refusal in silence. Neither wrote a fallback; an unhandled union arm IS the fallback, and a false "submitted" on the surface whose job is explaining what happened is the exact failure the fail-loud rule exists to prevent. The guard scans every .ts/.tsx under src/dashboard and fails any module that names one refusal arm without the other; naming both in one condition is legal and clean, since that is exhaustive. Exempt: the fold itself (it is the thing being enforced) and src/dashboard/client/commands.ts, whose job is to PARSE the union rather than act on it. A negative control runs the walker against tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/command-result-unhandled-conflict.ts — the exact shipped shape — and against a clean both-arms condition, so a scan that resolved nothing cannot report the tree clean. Track D row D3 (2026-08-21) added the SECOND arm: "one arm without the other" is trivially satisfied by a module that names NEITHER — it posts a command, ignores the answer entirely, and every refusal lands on the success path in silence. All nine command-issuing surfaces now call the fold, so a module under src/dashboard/** that calls .executeCommand( must IMPORT src/dashboard/app/command-result.js. The IMPORT is what is checked rather than a mention of the function name, because a comment explaining the fold would otherwise clear the very module that ignores it (that is the first thing this arm caught); an imported-but-uncalled binding is refused by eslint --max-warnings 0. Its own negative control is tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/command-result-unfolded-dispatch.ts, plus a posts-and-folds string and a posts-nothing string that must both read clean.

guards.name: roadmap-doc-binding
guards.invariant: D263/D326/D329 (roadmap §Governance; ref guards-and-tests): the plan's two forms are bound to each other BOTH ways, mechanically. The prose in docs/rebuild/** is normative and the tree in docs/roadmap/roadmap.md is its machine-readable form and the operator's tracking view, so a rename on either side must fail this gate instead of rotting into two plans that disagree. Six arms, all decided by ONE pure function of (planText, files) so the real tree and every fixture go through identical code. (a) Every doc: ref on every node resolves: a phase ref (03.2) names exactly one docs/rebuild/03.2-*.md, a reference ref (ref:write-safety) names docs/rebuild/reference/write-safety.md, and a §section matches a heading's NUMBER (§5.4, §5 for '## 5. …'), its TEXT exactly (the phase docs number no headings, so §Phase summary is the only way to cite one) or, for a range (§14.1–14.2), both endpoints as numbers; a refusal names the file, the section and the headings it nearly matched, because 'no such section' alone is a sentence nobody can act on (D261). (b) Every <!-- roadmap: id --> tag and every <!-- roadmap-status: id --> block in docs/rebuild/** (including migrations/; excluding history/, reviews/, findings/, and guides/) names a node the plan declares — asserted by CALLING the generator's own bindDocsToPlan rather than restating its rule, so the site and the gate can never refuse different things (D252), and by proving the guard's scan is byte-identical to scanDocs'. (e) Every builds: line carries a layer tag; parsePlan refuses one that does not, and the arm is belt-and-braces over the parsed shape because a Feature may still be a bare string in the schema. (f) Phase 3 is exactly 3.1 → 3.2 → 3.3 → 3.4, each part requires its predecessor, every immediate task uses consecutive chronological numbering, and same-number hyphenated tasks are a complete prior-wave-dependent parallel wave whose cards declare dedicated worktrees. Arms (c) and (d) ship as RATCHETS declared IN the test file: ALLOW_MISSING_DOC_REF and ALLOW_UNTAGGED are EMPTY and must stay so. A ratchet only shrinks: an allowlisted id whose gap has closed fails as stale, and one naming no node at all fails as a rename rather than a closed gap. Nine checked-in fixtures under tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/roadmap-binding/ are miniature repos with the same docs/ layout, read by the same collector as the repo: clean, dangling-phase-doc, dangling-section, unknown-reference-slug, tag-names-no-node, status-names-no-node, node-without-doc-ref, node-with-no-tag and builds-without-layer. D326 adds live-tree mutations that swap chronological tasks and remove a parallel task's worktree declaration. Every negative is asserted to fail with a message naming the ref, tag, id, task or part, and the clean tree is asserted non-empty in both directions — a walker that resolved nothing would otherwise report every arm green.

guards.name: workflow-layout

guards.invariant: D312/D316/D317 (ref workflow-model §§1.6, 1.6.1, 2026-09-02): the retired authoring path stays dead and the simplicity budget has no escape hatch. `workflow-layout` owns the FOLDER shape; this guard owns what an author WRITES. AST, never text, so a comment mentioning `flow(` passes. (c) WORKFLOW-KEYED GENERIC ADAPTER (D316): under `src/dashboard/`, `src/server/` and `src/services/` (tests excluded) any string literal EQUAL to a registered workflow id is refused, naming its syntactic context — an equality comparison, a case label, a dispatch-table key, a workflow-keyed call argument — unless it is one of nine reviewed exact `(file, workflow id)` pairs, each citing the decision the site's own comments name: `src/server/dry-run-scenario/compose.ts` and `src/server/dry-run-scenario/manifests.ts` × (`separations`, `separations-kuali-finalization`, `person-lookup`) for D318 / ref guards-and-tests §10.9's one T1b manifest-loader and target-resolver registration surface; `src/server/dashboard/compose.ts` / `separations` for D289's receipt-comparison registry sealed against the current separations descriptor; and `src/server/dashboard/projectors/run-queue-projection.ts` / `separations` plus `src/server/activity-person-pseudonym-backfill/service.ts` / `separations` for D288, whose Activity person-pseudonym evidence is current-Separations-only by decision. An entry whose reason cites no decision, and an entry the scan no longer matches, are both refused — staleness is this arm's negative control, since a scanner that resolved nothing would report every entry stale. Any other repository-visible file under `src/workflows/`, `tests/scenario/` or `docs/rebuild/migrations/` ATTRIBUTED to a registered workflow is refused by path, naming that workflow's own budget — an owner that failed to resolve throws rather than printing a plausible `its workflow.ts`. Attribution has TWO rules, because D265 rule 3 puts a harness INSIDE the step it proves and leaves the harness id out of the path entirely: under `src/workflows/` a file belongs to the registered FOLDER it sits in — `workflowSourceFolder`, from that same one derivation, longest folder prefix wins — so `src/workflows/separations/identity-check/module.ts` is `separations-identity-check`'s budget and never the composition's; everywhere else a whole directory segment or the basename stem that equals a registered id, or begins with one followed by `-`, `_` or `.`, attributes to the LONGEST such id, so `tests/scenario/separations-kuali-read.scenario.test.ts` belongs to the harness while `tests/scenario/separations-extra/foo.ts` and `docs/rebuild/migrations/separations_extra.md` stay `separations`'s budget instead of suffixing their way out of the arm. Both rules, and the two `undefined` answers, are asserted directly. Two closed, staleness-checked exemptions — `docs/rebuild/migrations/separations-legacy-behavior.md` as the migration record's own overflow (D312) and `tests/scenario/dashboard/separations/` as ref guards-and-tests §10.11/§10.12 T2/T3 dashboard proofs, which §1.6.1 admits because a genuinely new DASHBOARD capability is not reuse-only workflow authoring — and one closed pre-canonical structural-scenario allowlist for the four chunk harnesses still at `tests/scenario/<id>.scenario.test.ts` (D318 / §10.4); a workflow carrying both a canonical and a pre-canonical structural scenario is refused as two. Twenty-four violating fixtures, each written to a temp root and read back by the same collector: retired-recipe-type-anywhere-in-the-program, retired-node-fragment-factory-in-a-test, retired-workflow-recipe-specifier, a-file-named-recipe-ts, bare-recipe-identifier-inside-the-authoring-seam, flow-builder-imported-and-called-beside-workflow-ts, flow-builder-imported-three-levels-up-from-a-step-folder, descriptor-hand-authored-under-src-workflows, stores-composed-inside-a-workflow-folder, two-defineWorkflow-calls-in-one-workflow-file, generic-server-branch-keyed-by-workflow-id, generic-dashboard-dispatch-table-keyed-by-workflow-id, allowlisted-file-branching-on-a-DIFFERENT-workflow-id, another-file-branching-on-an-allowlisted-workflow-id, stale-D316-allowlist-entry, uncited-D316-allowlist-entry, fifth-authored-artifact-for-a-workflow, fifth-artifact-under-tests-scenario, fifth-artifact-inside-a-harness-folder-belongs-to-the-harness, fifth-artifact-in-a-folder-suffixing-a-registered-id, fifth-artifact-whose-stem-suffixes-a-registered-id-with-an-underscore, two-structural-scenarios-for-one-workflow, stale-artifact-exemption, stale-pre-canonical-structural-scenario. Those two arm-(c) fixtures, plus a passing assertion for the reviewed pair itself, are the pair-EXACTNESS proof: ONE reviewed `(src/server/dashboard/compose.ts, solo)` entry held constant across three trees, which a file-keyed allowlist fails on the first and an id-keyed allowlist on the second. guards.name: duo-ceremony-lease
guards.invariant: Ref execution-and-sessions §10 (D267): no login path reaches the UCSD SSO form or the Duo WebAuthn assertion without presenting a DuoCeremonyLeaseToken, and one credential admits one Duo ceremony at a time. The token is minted and retired ONLY by the lease store (src/infra/sqlite/authority-database.ts, through src/base/duo-ceremony-lease.ts's module-private WeakSets); the brand is conjured by `as`/`satisfies` nowhere outside that module; defineVerifiedLoginRecipe (src/infra/browser/authenticated-application.ts) is the ONE caller of the gate's withCeremony; every store login recipe is the wrapper's {navigate, ceremony} shape rather than a single flow, and every SSO-helper call in a store presents `token`. Duo's signature counter is per CREDENTIAL while Duo Autopilot's copy is per browser PROFILE, so two ceremonies in one second present the same floored counter and Duo reads the non-advancing one as a cloned key — which BURNS the profile (D243). Each arm runs against tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/duo-lease-recipe-violation.ts, the exact pre-lease recipe shape, so a walker that resolved nothing cannot report the tree clean.

guards.name: step-omission-invariants
guards.invariant: D307: an operator may omit a timeline step at start and type the facts it would have read; only a step folder's own declared `omission` may say what a TASK node of that step would have produced, gates and transactions are never substituted, and ALWAYS-GATE (D77) is a planner invariant, not a per-descriptor promise. The production registry declares three omissions, all on `separations` — `kronos-timecard`, `ucpath-transaction` and `kuali-finalization`, each authored in its own step folder's `omission.ts` and carried onto the descriptor by that folder's `nodes.category(..., { omission })` — and every sweep here pins those three BY NAME plus the one in-test fixture declaration, asserting at the end that it visited EXACTLY that set, so a deleted, renamed or unwired production declaration turns the sweep red instead of quietly shrinking it. The fixture (a read, the `identity-approval` operator gate, a post-gate task and a transaction, across `reading`/`identity-check`/`writing`) exists only for the arms the registry cannot reach: the definition-time refusals, which no registered descriptor may contain and still import, and the `blocked` cascade arm Separations has no instance of. (a) `defineWorkflowDescriptor` throws at DEFINITION TIME when an omission's `produces` names a gate or a transaction node of its own step — proved for both kinds, and separately for a form that declares a duplicate field key; (b) every production omittable step's `stepOmissionCascade` row equals its exact pinned row (Separations: three `{ state: "omittable", forces: [] }` rows), while the fixture keeps the `omittable`-or-`blocked` union assertion, since letting the real cascade run un-caught is what proves it never throws for any refusal but `dependency-omitted`; (c) every RAW step-folder declaration (`KRONOS_TIMECARD_OMISSION` and its two siblings, imported from the `omission.ts` modules themselves rather than read back off an already-parsed `spec.form`) parses through `StepOmissionFormSchema` with the exact pinned field keys, no duplicate key and exactly the pinned `produces` node ids, and the registry is reconciled against that pinned set in BOTH directions, so a folder that stops wiring its declaration through `nodes.category` is red too; (d) `planStepOmissions`, driven with the cascade's own exported placeholder facts (`stepOmissionPlaceholderFacts`), never classifies ANY gate node as `asserted` or `omitted` in three plan shapes per declaration — the step alone, the step together with its cascade `forces` set, and every omittable step of the descriptor at once — with Separations' `identity-approval` gate required to be present and to EXECUTE (classified neither way, under a refusal-free plan) in all three, and each production plan's node classification pinned: `dates` and `receipt` are the only asserted nodes, while `timecard-search`, `timecard`, `clear-pending`, `file-termination` and `finalize-kuali` are only ever omitted. There is no separate "no separations omission produces identity-approval" arm: a declaration naming the gate throws at import, so that assertion could not fail; the invariant lives in (c)'s exact `produces` pinning and (d)'s planner sweep.
